title: Methangen H-Cell Setup
author: Annette Rowe
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.88vhzw6
materials: Autoclaving and Purging of reactors: Once reactors assembled (minus caps and electrodes) I autoclave with media in the reactor (note I separate media into two components for autoclaving and I only autoclave with component A). This is different than other protocols I have seen but I feel it is more anaerobic and better for the PEMs. Autoclave with ¾ volume of component A (cover with a loose normal bottle cap) in the reactors. Autoclave component B Separately (usually autoclave all in first round but can aliquot in case of time restrictions. All reactors gassed with N2/CO2 80/20. Usually takes around 10 min to be anaerobic. Post purge Attach stoppers and open screw caps (red anaerobic for working electrode) and blue (smaller hole punch) for the counter/reference. Place in the anaerobic chamber overnight. Run abiotic CV’s DPV’s etc. 6:Inoculating reactors: I perform the equivalent of a 10% biomass transfer for electrochemical experiments. From stationary phase methanol grown cultures (~OD600 1.0) I centrifuge 10 mL to add to electrochemical cells. I use a centrifuge in an anaerobic chamber. I do 6 2-mL aliquots and save one 2 ml sample for protein analysis. Each 2-mL aliquot is centrifuges at 8,000 G for 5 min. Spent media is removed. (This spent media can be added to a reactor as a spent media control. As a not I recommend centrifuging media longer as the cells do not all pellet in 5 min though the majority do, I have had a few spent media controls make methane) Cells are re-suspended in media from each electrochemical cell (I remove prior to resuspension with a syringe through one of the septa) and then reinjected via septa into the working electrode chamber. I have washed cells in the past, but have found that one wash is sufficient to remove spent media and additional washes usually result in stress on cells and/or loss of biomass. From this point I generally run chronoamperometry ~-500 mV SHE for at least 48 hours before performing any electrochemical experiments. If you are quantifying methane I suggest taking a time zero sample to control for background methane in chamber or dissolved in spent media.

steps.title: Clean Glassware
steps.instruction: Clean all glassware using soap and DI water, performing periodic acid washing.

steps.title: Clean and Protonate PEM
steps.instruction: Prepare the proton exchange membrane (PEM) according to the MFC protocol.

substeps.instruction: Low boil (~80°C) for 30min-1hr with DI water.
Store in DI water until use.

steps.title: Prepare Electrodes
steps.instruction: Sterilize and prepare the working and counter electrodes.

substeps.instruction: Autoclave working and counter electrodes for each reactor in a separate covered bin.
Attach the working electrode (carbon cloth) via titanium wire across a thick black high pressure anaerobic stopper.
Prepare the titanium/platinum counter electrode using white stoppers with potential for three holes (keep only one open for the reference electrode).
Flame titanium to remove organics between use.
Ethanol and UV sterilize reference electrodes.

steps.title: Assemble H-Cell Reactor
steps.instruction: Assemble the reactor components, ensuring the proton exchange membrane is supported between the two sides.

substeps.instruction: Position the PEM between the two sides of the reactor using the open circle flatten ports.
Attach the white plastic fitting complete with O-ring.
Attach red caps and stoppers to the side ports.
Secure the assembly with a plastic chain clamp.
